value:
APPLY_PATCH NOW HAS DIRECT TEST COVERAGE. Every other test in tools/gdl/tests/test_webfrank.py exercises the STAGE functions in isolation; apply_patch's own orchestration -- stage ordering, the post-recolor preconditions, the relocation-set re-derivation between stages, the deferred exit-dead checks and the closing hash assert -- was reachable only by running the real ninja build against real objects, so a guard bug there would have surfaced as somebody's build failure rather than as a red test. `_elf_object()` builds a minimal ELF32 big-endian relocatable object in memory (section headers at e_shoff 0x20 with e_shentsize/e_shnum/e_shstrndx at 0x2E/0x30/0x32; one PROGBITS .text; one RELA whose sh_info names .text and sh_link names .symtab; a SYMTAB whose sh_link names .strtab), taking relocations as (function-relative offset, symbol name, type, addend) and storing them at value+offset, the section-relative form _function_text_relocations reads back.

ONE FIXTURE DETAIL IS LOAD-BEARING and is the mistake to avoid if this is ever rewritten: .text must be PADDED by the symbol's value so the function does not sit at section offset 0. Without that padding every offset assertion passes vacuously and the fixture only ever tests the value == 0 case. One test deliberately uses a non-zero symbol value to pin it, and the padding bug is exactly what that test caught during development.

THE 12 TESTS (class ApplyPatchObjectTests), all calling apply_patch itself: the post-recolor permutation reaching the target end to end -- the named gap; a non-zero symbol value honoured; the three refusals that live ONLY in apply_patch and nowhere in the stage functions (a post-recolor permutation REQUIRES a register stage, may NOT ride unproven_recolor_audit, and REFUSES any window carrying a relocation in either object); the companion positive that a relocation OUTSIDE the window does not trip that refusal; input-hash drift, target-hash drift, a missing target object and a target/current size mismatch all failing closed; and a pre-recolor permutation whose relocation rides its atom, asserted by reading the REWRITTEN relocation table back out of the patched object -- a property apply_patch owns and that permute_instruction_atoms alone cannot demonstrate.

THE CENSUS COLUMN, AND A BUG THAT MATTERS MORE. tools/gdl/composed_census/wf_census.py gains destination_agreement(), dstok/dstrc columns, a totals line, and a roster sort that ranks by structural debt first and then by destination agreement descending. Destination agreement is the real tractability axis: a copy-form site whose DESTINATION already agrees is a pure form change dischargeable by the plain proof modes, while one whose destination differs is a form change AND a recolor at once, needs the combined class, and is justified only by a machine-proven renaming. The per-site classes encoded this all along; nothing aggregated it, so the roster could not be ranked by it.

BUT the tool COULD NOT RUN AT ALL. It computed ROOT as one level above tools/gdl/composed_census/ (i.e. tools/gdl), so sys.path.insert(ROOT/tools/gdl) pointed at a non-existent tools/gdl/tools/gdl and both build/ paths were wrong; it died on `import webfrank` from any directory. It has been unrunnable since it was promoted out of lane scratch. This is precisely the failure AGENTS.md discipline 17 warns about, and it argues the discipline needs teeth: a promoted script should have to be RUN ONCE FROM THE REPO ROOT before the promoting commit lands. Recommend adding that sentence to discipline 17.

FIRST MEASUREMENT off the repaired tool, image-wide over 2837 equal-size paired functions: 9010 `other` words, 8061 `regfield`, and only 97 copy-form sites in the entire image -- of which just 7 (7.2%) have a destination that already agrees. The cheap pure-form-change population is effectively exhausted; 90 of the 97 remaining copy-form sites need the combined form+recolor class. All five shipped-rule canaries remain visible from raw bodies.
